content:
Points, lines, angles, polygons and circles — Basic Geometrical Ideas builds the vocabulary every later geometry chapter depends on, and the Olympiad tests it with precise definitions and angle arithmetic. Here is what it covers, with a free 10-question test with figures.

What the Class 6 Maths Olympiad Basic Geometrical Ideas chapter tests

  • Points, lines, rays, segments and curves
  • Angles, complements and supplements
  • Polygons, diagonals, triangles and quadrilaterals
  • Circle parts: radius, diameter, chord, arc, sector

Key facts your child should know

  • Exactly ONE line passes through two distinct points.
  • Complementary angles add to 90°; supplementary to 180°.
  • Diagonals of an n-gon = n(n − 3)/2 — a hexagon has 9.
  • The diameter is the longest chord: d = 2r.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Mixing up complement (90°) and supplement (180°).
  • Counting sides as diagonals in polygons.
  • Calling a radius a chord (a chord joins two points ON the circle).
